title: Support for Singapore water technology firms going overseas
asked: Mr Dennis Tan asked whether the Government has assessed the export potential of Singapore's water recycling and integrated water management capabilities, and whether it plans a coordinated strategy to position Singapore firms as global leaders in the sector. He also asked whether existing financing and risk-sharing mechanisms are sufficient for local water-tech firms to compete internationally on large-scale overseas projects, and whether further enhancements are planned to support them in securing international desalination and recycling contracts.
response: Mr Alvin Tan said water supply is an existential issue and the Government has promoted the water industry and invested in water technology R&D under RIE. He said Enterprise Singapore, PUB and the Singapore Water Association support companies such as Keppel and Sembcorp overseas, and cited the Singapore International Water Week and business missions. He listed grants including the Enterprise Development Grant, Market Readiness Assistance grant and Enterprise Financing Scheme, with risk sharing for overseas expansion, and said enhancements were announced at Budget and MTI COS. He said there are no immediate plans for a circular economy export office or integrated cooling solutions, but PUB has test-bedding support and the Living Lab fund; since 2006 about $800 million from RIE has gone to water tech, with the industry growing from 50 to about 400 companies and over 20,000 jobs.

key_points.point: The Government has promoted the water industry and invested in water technology R&D under RIE.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: the Government has been promoting the water industry and investing in the research and development (R&D) of water technologies under Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE)

key_points.point: Enterprise Singapore, PUB and the Singapore Water Association support companies such as Keppel and Sembcorp overseas.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: Enterprise Singapore, PUB and the Singapore Water Association work together to support Singapore-based companies such as Keppel and Sembcorp as they build capabilities and pursue opportunities overseas

key_points.point: Watertech companies can tap the Enterprise Development Grant and Market Readiness Assistance grant.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: Watertech companies like Hydroleap and SG Enviro have and can tap the Enterprise Development Grant to upgrade, innovate and access new markets and our Market Readiness Assistance grant to defray the costs of overseas market promotion

key_points.point: The Enterprise Financing Scheme offers risk sharing with participating financial institutions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: Under EFS, Government offers risk sharing with participating Financial Institutions, such as for fixed asset loans for construction or the acquisition of plants and equipment

key_points.point: There are no immediate plans for a circular economy export office or integrated cooling solutions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: With regard to the circular economy export office and the market integrated cooling solutions, there are no immediate plans to do so

key_points.point: PUB has a Living Lab fund providing R&D funding for test-bedding.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: they have this Living Lab fund which provides R&D funding

key_points.point: Since 2006, about $800 million from RIE has been invested in water tech.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: Since 2006, Government has invested about $800 million from RIE on water tech

key_points.point: The water tech industry has grown from 50 to about 400 companies.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: we have now moved from 50 to about 400 companies and increased job opportunities

key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: now, it is about over 20,000 jobs

key_points.point: Schemes including the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation and EFS were enhanced.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: We have enhanced the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation grant, and we have also enhanced the EFS

key_points.point: Hydroleap expanded to Australia and Thailand, including a partnership in PepsiCo Thailand.
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: It is now expanded to Australia. It is expanded to Thailand, for example, partnering with the Bangkok Industrial Gas, to provide smart water treatment solutions in PepsiCo Thailand

left_open: Whether existing financing and risk-sharing mechanisms are sufficient for Singapore-based water-tech firms to compete internationally with state-backed competitors in large-scale overseas projects.
Whether a coordinated strategy will be developed to position Singapore firms as global leaders in the water sector.
Whether further enhancements are planned specifically to help local firms secure international desalination and recycling contracts.
Whether the Government will use more government-to-government platforms to pre-qualify or support Singapore water technologies in emerging markets.
Whether a sovereign project bond or risk-sharing mechanism with a Team Singapore guarantee will be introduced for larger overseas desalination projects.
supplementary: Further support mechanisms and market strategies for Singapore water technology firms overseas.
